neet_che_u14_t06_1.working: CH3+ has three bonding pairs and no lone pair, so carbon has only 6 valence electrons. It is sp2 hybridised and trigonal planar, with an empty p orbital.

neet_che_u14_t06_2.working: Alkyl groups donate electrons by the +I effect and destabilise a carbanion. Stability therefore falls with more substitution: methyl > 1° > 2° > 3°.

neet_che_u14_t06_3.working: The cationic carbon has three alpha carbons: two CH3 (6 H) and one CH2 (2 H). That gives 6 + 2 = 8 alpha hydrogens.

neet_che_u14_t06_4.working: A is true because the three methyl groups stabilise the cation by hyperconjugation and the +I effect. R is a true structural fact but does not explain the stability order. Both true, R not the explanation (intended answer).

neet_che_u14_t06_5.working: Statement I is correct: the allylic cation is stabilised by pi conjugation and by hyperconjugation from the methyl C-H bonds. Statement II is incorrect: allylic and benzylic carbanions become sp2 and planar so the lone pair can delocalise.
